text:
Alex M: quick q — go client getting 401 when starting a streaming request. api key comes from a docker secret mounted at /run/secrets/redwood_key. we do `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=$(cat /run/secrets/redwood_key)` and then use it in header. any quick checks for trailing newline or encoding gotchas?

Rachel L: super common. first quick check: `cat -A /run/secrets/redwood_key` or `xxd -g 1 -u -l 64 /run/secrets/redwood_key` to reveal \`^M\` or extra \`\n\`. also `od -c` is handy.

Samir: in go i usually do: 
```go
b, _ := os.ReadFile("/run/secrets/redwood_key")
apiKey := strings.TrimRight(string(b), "\r\n")
// then build header
req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Basic "+base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString([]byte(apiKey+":")))
```
TrimRight is safer than TrimSpace if you only want to remove EOLs.

Alex M: ah ok — we were using strings.TrimSpace earlier. could that remove intentional leading/trailing spaces people expect?

Rachel L: yeah TrimSpace removes tabs/spaces too; usually fine but if a key legitimately starts/ends with space (rare) it could be bad. prefer explicit TrimRight for CR/LF.

Samir: also watch base64: if the raw key has a `\n` it will end up encoded and the receiving gateway can reject the auth early (401) before streaming starts. for quick curl sanity:
```bash
# use printf not echo so no extra newline
curl -v -H "Authorization: Basic $(printf '%s' \"$KEY\" | base64)" https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams
```
If you use `echo $KEY | base64` you might get an extra newline depending on shell.

Taylor: adding CI gotcha: windows runner artifacts can introduce CRLF. in GH Actions, do `tr -d '\r' < secretfile > secretfile.fixed` or add `apiKey = strings.TrimRight(apiKey, "\\r\\n")` in code. Also added a tiny helper in our SDK to normalize keys on init.

Alex M: thanks all — i'll push a tiny change to use TrimRight + unit test that writes a file with CRLF and ensures header length matches. pinging @Rachel L for review.

Rachel L: :thumbsup: will review in a bit.
